experiment: P5l fixed-minibatch CUDA-compute-guarded shared frozen-forward and dense bounded-head execution
research_question: With the P5g mechanism unchanged, does one shared frozen base forward preserve complete full-pool outputs exactly and reduce guarded per-inference-batch latency relative to two frozen base forwards?
single_changed_axis: The only change from P5k is timing unit: exactness remains on every 3,780-example paired-power pool, while latency is measured on the pre-registered first complete 126-example batch. This separates semantic equivalence from the operational per-batch cost and shortens the GPU-exclusive window.

execution.benchmark_batch: first complete index-ordered batch, indices 0 through 125, no data-dependent sampling
execution.reference: two frozen base forwards plus unchanged dense attachment
execution.candidate: one frozen base forward plus identical unchanged dense attachment
execution.timing: CUDA synchronize before and after each run; before and after full-equivalence calls and every warmup/repeat reject any external Python PID whose nvidia-smi pmon process type contains C

pre_generation_amendment.reason: The initial draft used seeds larger than the unsigned 32-bit MATLAB RNG domain. No P5l data, model inference, test data or result was created with that draft. Before generation, all seeds are replaced by unused in-domain values; no scientific mechanism, gate, split role, model or benchmark definition changes.

development_data.roles: evaluation-only; no training, selection, calibration or threshold adjustment

stop_rule: Any exception or external Python CUDA-compute PID at a guard checkpoint freezes accessed P5l identities without result. Any equivalence or latency failure stops P5l with no threshold, head, weight, feature, batch, scheduling, compiler or quantization change and no confirmation.

confirmation_if_and_only_if_development_.decision: Only a pass supports a narrow frozen-execution per-batch cost claim, never a new architecture or classification claim.
